contracts: Verification succeeds only when every applicable Consumer has structured successful-enable evidence tied to its real production call surface; it fails if any Consumer is missing, simulated, or unsuccessful.

Test-author entry: scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s21.py. Create real tests for every assertion in this slice, using @pytest.mark.cer_assertion for exact assertion IDs. Read the actual production behavior and bound oracle. Never create unconditional RED, skip/xfail, empty cases or prewritten execution receipts. Missing markers are authoring work; only an actual probe decides present/missing.
selector_intents: Run the mapped cases against the unchanged real production owner. Required observable: A targeted Toolchain test or runtime probe invokes each applicable Consumer's production call surface and emits structured per-Consumer successful-enable evidence. Required result: For every applicable Consumer, enable is executed through its real production call surface and structured evidence identifies the Consumer, call-surface identity, operation, and successful result. Emit CER-A-5D0751923C06-BEHAVIOR only immediately before a genuine assertion failure demonstrating this unmet behavior. Do not emit it for setup/import/timeout/missing-marker failures, and do not force already-present behavior to fail.
Select a negative validator path that substitutes a mock, stub, simulated dispatch, or direct state mutation for the Consumer real call surface, and fail when that substitution is accepted.
Select the targeted real-Consumer execution test or probe and fail when any applicable Consumer lacks a production call-surface invocation or successful enable evidence.
